findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Paper plates were observed with the food contact surfaces up/exposed. Education was conducted and they were flipped over to correct.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed moist rags stored on the counter in multiple locations throughout the facility. PIC was made aware and the rags were returned to the sanitizer buckets to correct the violation. Ensure that wiping clothes are stored inside the sanitizer bucket with sanitizer solution when cloths are not in use.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).[C]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed dishes to not be inverted above the cook line. PIC was made aware and will have staff invert the dishes on this shelf. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are protected during storage.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the gasket on the walk in freezer in the basement to be falling off causing the door to not seal properly. PIC was made aware and will make arrangements to get the gasket repaired. Ensure that equipment is maintained in a state of repair that meets the manufactures standards.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety foods held past their seven day date marking period:
1) Mushrooms sauce in the downstairs walk in cooler (dated 4/16)
2) French onion soup in the downstairs walk in cooler (dated 4/15)
3) Creme brulée in the upstairs standing cooler (next to the grill) (dated 4/16)
4) Roasted duck in the ground level walk in cooler (dated 4/16)
5) Mushroom sauce in the ground level walk in cooler (dated 4/14)
CORRECTED- the aforementioned foods will be discarded. Continue educating staff about date marking requirements and holding times. Ensure all TCS foods are marked to be used or DISCARDED within seven days (the day of preparation counts as DAY ONE).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods lacking date marking throughout the facility:
1) FIRST REPEAT: The standing pass through cooler contained cooked noodles and freshly prepared sauces.
2) The walk in meat cooler contained minestrone and French onion soup.
3) The two door standing cooler contained multiple sauces and in house prepared foods.
CORRECTED- items were marked with the date of preparation (being either Saturday 4/18 or Wed. 4/15). Foods marked 4/15 (downstairs walk in cooler) must be used or discarded today. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are date marked to be used or discarded within SEVEN days. The date of preparation counts as day one.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5ºC (41ºF) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be in disrepair:
1) The gaskets of the ground level walk in cooler are frayed.
2) The gaskets of the pass through cooler on the kitchen line are frayed and deteriorating. 
3) The shelves of the standing freezer on the south side of the kitchen line contain rust.
Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained smooth and easily cleanable to prevent the contamination of foods. Replace gaskets and either repaint or replace shelves by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the downstairs hand washing sink nearest the stairs to be leaking water just below the basin. Once water passes the basin it is considered waste water. Ensure repairs are made by law to properly convey the waste water on or by 4/24/26.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facilities to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) The fan covers of the ground level walk in cooler contain an accumulation of dust. 
2) The floor in the Southeast corner of the server line contains an accumulation of food debris.
3) The floor next to the basement water heater needs cleaned more frequently to better monitor potential pests.
Ensure physical facilities and nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Inspector observed the internal surface of the coffee machine to be soiled. PIC was made aware. A staff member was instructed to clean the internal surface of the coffee machine. Inspector later reexamine the area mentioned and it was cleaned to sight of touch. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the internal surface of the coffee machine are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.


Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Inspector observed food stocks in a few storage containers stored in the standing refrigerator at the entrance of the kitchen without proper date marking. Inspector inquired about the prep timeline of the stocks and PIC informed inspector that they were made the day before. PIC instructed a staff member to properly date mark the items in the cooler. Ensure that food items are often date marked if they are not consumed or used within 24-hour of prep.


 Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Inspector observed a build up of ice at the door of the meat walk-in freezer that is adjoining the meat walk-in cooler in the basement. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the ice accumulation is cleaned up providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: Inspector observed an employee take something off of the bottom of his shoe, throw it away and then pick up a wiping cloth to continue labeling pans off food. The employee was stopped and coached on the missed hand washing opportunity and washed his hands properly. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Inspector observed a bottle of wine in the ice bin with ice for drinks. The bottle was removed from the ice, the ice was removed from the bin and the ice bin sanitized. Never store bottle in ice used for food. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

(A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: Facility has routine pest control. The pest control logs show no pests caught in traps anywhere in the facility. However, rodent droppings are observed on the long white wood shelves across from the vegetable walk in cooler. These shelves must be maintained clean and monitored daily for signs of activity. If there are any signs of pests the PCO should be notified immediately. The facility just went to monthly service from by weekly service. The PCO was informed during the inspection today and they will be out this afternoon to do a thorough evaluation of the building. There is no evidence of damaged food. However, droppings are considered evidence of presence. Ensure that premise is inspected daily by staff to ensure that proper cleaning and exclusion is taking place.

PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: Inspector observed the seal on the reach in cooler on the end of the cook line to be in disrepair. Replace the seal.

 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Inspector observed the floor to the right of the cook line by the wall to have food debris. Also the floor at the ramp to the other building in the basement is soiled with soda syrup. Clean these floors and maintain them clean. 
Also, the bottom shelf of the reach in freezer on the prep side of the line is soiled. Clean and maintain coolers clean. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
